subject: Request: PO requirement exception for PilotPartner pilot engagement
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@pilotpartner.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@pilotpartner.ai
Date: 2025-06-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Small pilot — PO process question

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday — excited to run a 6-week pilot with Redwood. We're a pre-Series A company and our finance team typically issues invoices (Net 30) rather than going through buyer PO systems. The pilot is scoped at $4,500 (see attached SOW).

Is Redwood able to accept our standard Net 30 invoice for this pilot rather than requiring a PO? If a PO is mandatory, can we get an expedited one-time PO so we can start this week?

I attached the SOW. Happy to complete any onboarding paperwork you need.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Partnerships | PilotPartner
sofia@pilotpartner.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: PilotPartner_SOW_v1.pdf

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@pilotpartner.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Small pilot — PO process question

Hi Sofia — thanks for sending the SOW and for the demo follow-up.

Quick answers: Redwood's default policy requires a Purchase Order for any supplier relationship that will be invoiced and tracked in our ERP — that helps with accounting, tax, and audit controls. However, we do have an exceptions path for pilot/early-stage vendors under a $5k threshold where a one-time finance exception can be made.

To move fast, can you do the following?
- Fill the vendor onboarding form (I can attach a blank copy if helpful) — we need W-9 or equivalent tax docs and company address.
- Confirm billing remit details on the invoice (email to accounting@redwood.ai).
- Confirm the SOW total (you indicated $4,500) and that there are no recurring charges beyond the pilot.

I'll loop in Marcus (finance) and Laura (procurement lead) so they can confirm whether we can approve a one-time PO-less invoice for this pilot. If not, Marcus can issue a one-time PO fast-track.

I'll attach the vendor onboarding form filled by our side after you confirm.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai

Attachment: Vendor_Onboarding_Form_filled.pdf

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <sofia@pilotpartner.ai>
Date: 2025-06-13T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Small pilot — PO process question

Grace / Sofia —

Thanks — quick finance perspective: our standard control is that any payable recorded in the general ledger should be tied to a PO unless it meets an approved exception. Exceptions are limited and require documented justification + procurement sign-off. Thresholds: under $2k typically handled as P-card or ad-hoc; $2k-$10k can be eligible for a one-time invoice exception with procurement approval. Given this is $4.5k, we can approve a one-time exception but need the following to complete the audit trail:

1) Completed Vendor Onboarding Form (including ACH/W-9) — we'll need an electronically signed copy.
2) The signed SOW (you've already attached that, thanks).
3) A short justification (1-2 lines) from Partnerships on business rationale (pilot -> strategic evaluation for potential expansion).

If you can provide docs today, finance will issue an exception code and allow accounting to process a Net 30 invoice without creating a PO. If any recurring billing starts, we will require a formal PO and vendor setup in Coupa.

If Sofia prefers a PO, we can fast-track a one-time PO; that process typically takes 24 hours once onboarding is complete.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Finance Business Partner | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

--
Note: Please send invoices to accounting@redwood.ai and include DL-2025-0847 as reference.

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@pilotpartner.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@pilotpartner.ai
Date: 2025-06-13T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Small pilot — PO process question

Thanks Marcus / Grace — appreciate the clarity.

Attached: signed SOW and our vendor onboarding PDF (filled). We will also send a W-9 to accounting@redwood.ai and put DL-2025-0847 on the invoice. Business justification: Pilot aims to validate integration of PilotPartner routing for Redwood's Dedicated customers; potential expansion to Dedicated customers in Q3 if successful.

We prefer to proceed on Net 30 invoice terms to avoid delay in our cash flow. If procurement still requires a PO, please proceed with the fast-track PO and let us know any forms we missed.

Best,
Sofia

Attachments: PilotPartner_SOW_v1_signed.pdf, Vendor_Onboarding_Form_filled.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramos <sofia@pilotpartner.ai>
Date: 2025-06-16T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: one-time invoice exception (PilotPartner, DL-2025-0847)

Hi team —

Procurement has reviewed the submitted materials (signed SOW, onboarding form, W-9 sent to accounting). Given the pilot value ($4,500) and clear business case, I approve a one-time PO exemption for this engagement with the following conditions:

- Exception covers one invoice up to $4,800 total; any overages require re-approval.
- Pilot must be strictly time-boxed to the SOW (6 weeks).
- If there is a plan for recurring services after the pilot, vendor must be fully onboarded into Coupa and a standard PO must be issued before any recurring invoices.
- Finance will assign exception code EXC-2025-PP-01; accounting to process Net 30 invoice once charge is coded.

Sofia, you can send the invoice to accounting@redwood.ai referencing DL-2025-0847 and EXC-2025-PP-01. Grace, I'll update the procurement exceptions log and attach the approval PDF.

Laura Bennett
Procurement Lead | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: approved_exemption_record_20250616.pdf
